quote: Aber auch automorphe Funktion 2er Variabel mit binären Substitution (z. B. meine schon lange gesuchte Verallge- meinerung der Modulfunktionen, die bei ganzzahligen Substitutionen ungeändert bleiben) kann man wahrscheinlich so erhalten.
english: But automorphic functions of two variables with binary substitutions (e.g. my long-sought generalization of the modular functions, which remain unchanged under integral substitutions) can probably also be obtained this way.
topic: After a remark on a drop falling into a liquid, Hilbert proposes using Fuchs's independence of substitution coefficients from a parameter to build a general inversion problem, giving automorphic functions of two variables (ternary or binary substitutions), with an elliptic-integral example.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert is asking for meromorphic automorphic functions of two complex variables (z1, z2), each in the upper half-plane, that stay unchanged under a discrete group acting on both variables at once by binary fractional-linear substitutions with 'integral' coefficients. The natural reading is the Hilbert modular group SL2(O_K) of a real quadratic field K, where z_i -> (a_i z_i + b_i)/(c_i z_i + d_i) and (a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i) are the Galois conjugates of an integral matrix. This is the two-variable version of the elliptic modular functions, i.e. what are now called Hilbert modular functions and forms, living on Hilbert modular surfaces. The concrete conjecture on the page is narrower: that such functions can 'probably' be built from an inversion problem, using Fuchs's result that the substitution coefficients of a linear ODE do not depend on a parameter.
triage.answered_by: The theory of these functions came from Hilbert's own unpublished manuscript of 1893/94, which was worked out and published by his doctoral student Otto Blumenthal in his Habilitation 'Über Modulfunktionen von mehreren Veränderlichen' (Math. Ann. 56 (1903) 509–548 and 58 (1904) 497–527). Erich Hecke then developed it substantially in his 1910–1912 dissertation, and Shimura and others later built the arithmetic theory. The sources found do not show that Hilbert's specific suggested route (inversion via Fuchs's parameter-independent substitution coefficients) is how the functions were obtained. That particular method should be regarded as unconfirmed, not as realized.

evidence.claim: Blumenthal did the first pioneering work in a program outlined by Hilbert to create a theory of modular functions of several variables, meant to be as important as the one-variable theory.

The notion of a Hilbert modular form comes from David Hilbert's unpublished work and the habilitation thesis of his doctoral student Otto Blumenthal [Blu03]; Shimura later laid the foundation for the arithmetic theory.

Blumenthal had a manuscript by Hilbert from 1893/94 on the action of the modular group Γ_K of a totally real field K, and made it the basis of his Habilitation 'Über Modulfunktionen von mehreren Veränderlichen'.
Hilbert modular surfaces (Hilbert–Blumenthal surfaces) were first described by Blumenthal (1903, 1904) using unpublished notes by Hilbert.

Blumenthal's 1901 Göttingen Habilitationsschrift treated Hilbert modular forms for real quadratic fields, citing Hilbert's unpublished work of 1893–94; Hecke developed them significantly in his 1910 dissertation.
Reference: Blumenthal, O. Über Modulfunktionen von mehreren Veränderlichen. Math. Ann. 56:509–548 (1903) and 58:497–527 (1904).

triage.why: The phrase 'my long-sought generalization of the modular functions, which remain unchanged under integral substitutions', applied to automorphic functions of two variables under binary substitutions, matches what Hilbert worked on in 1893/94 and Blumenthal published in 1903–04: Hilbert modular functions. The object itself was clearly found and became a major theory. Hilbert modular forms and varieties are still an active research area, as current arXiv papers and LMFDB coverage show. It is not one of the 23 Paris problems, though it is connected to the 12th problem through complex multiplication. Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons. The identification rests on wording, since the diary entry is undated. And the specific conjecture that the functions come from a Fuchs-type inversion problem is not confirmed by any source found; the established construction followed Hilbert's manuscript, Blumenthal and Hecke, not that ODE route.
